title: We in the dot past: hablamos, comimos, vivimos; cuando; a menudo

cards.title: hablamos = we speak / we spoke
cards.body: For -ar verbs, the dot-past we form is the same as the present. Context, like the other half of the sentence, usually makes it clear. Cuando = when.

examples.en: When we speak, I understand everything.
When we spoke, I understood everything.
We spoke yesterday. / We'll speak tomorrow.

cards.title: esperamos; Spanglish to avoid
cards.body: Desesperado (desperate) comes from desesperar. English 'desperado' and 'no problemo' are mangled Spanish; it's ningún problema.

cards.title: -er: comemos → comimos; -ir: vivimos = vivimos
cards.body: In the past, -er verbs switch to -imos; -ir verbs look the same as the present.

cards.title: Present vs past in one sentence

examples.en: We always get lost, but we didn't get lost yesterday.
examples.es: Siempre nos perdemos, pero no nos perdimos ayer.

cards.title: a menudo = often
cards.body: Menudo (small, linked to 'minute') is literary, but a menudo is very common.

examples.en: We don't go out often, but we went out yesterday.
examples.es: No salimos a menudo, pero salimos ayer.
